records.name: Two-Digit Year Century Cutoff Pivot Policies

interpretation.description: Two-digit years (yy) must be mapped to four-digit century (yyyy). Different platforms have conflicting pivot windows.
interpretation.sas_policy: SAS default system option YEARCUTOFF specifies first year of 100-year span (typically YEARCUTOFF=1920 or 1926). With YEARCUTOFF=1920, 20 is 1920, 24 is 2024, 19 is 2019.
interpretation.python_policy: Python strptime %y maps 69-99 to 1969-1999, and 00-68 to 2000-2068 (POSIX standard).
interpretation.sql_policy: PostgreSQL YY format uses 2000-2099; RR format uses current year +/- 50 years.

ambiguity.reason: Conflicting century pivot between SAS YEARCUTOFF and Python %y produces silent 100-year errors for years around pivot boundary.

validation_rules: Explicitly pass century pivot formula during migration instead of relying on runtime defaults

records.name: Numeric Month/Day Permutation (01/02/2024)

interpretation.description: In US locale (en-US), '01/02/2024' represents January 2, 2024. In UK/Europe/International (en-GB), it represents February 1, 2024.
interpretation.resolution_policy: If both leading components are <= 12 and separated by '/' or '-', date is strictly ambiguous without external locale metadata.

ambiguity.reason: Indistinguishable without locale or schema format specifier.

validation_rules: Flag as UNCERTAIN unless format informat (e.g. MMDDYY vs DDMMYY) is explicitly declared in source

records.name: Unseparated Six-Digit String (010224)

interpretation.description: Can be interpreted as DDMMYY (01 Feb 2024), MMDDYY (02 Jan 2024), or YYMMDD (24 Feb 2001).
interpretation.resolution_policy: Requires source informat mapping (e.g., SAS informat DDMMYY6. vs MMDDYY6. vs YYMMDD6.).

ambiguity.reason: Three possible interpretations with conflicting day, month, and year assignments.

validation_rules: Never guess interpretation without source informat reference
